checks.label: In each successive time constant the value falls to 0.368 of the preceding value, so 0.632 of the remainder goes: a window one RC wide reads 0.368 for every R and C on the sliders, wherever it sits, and the line at its starting rate reaches zero exactly at its end

Separating puts every term in the dependent variable on one side and every term in the independent variable on the other: the rule becomes dv ÷ v = −dt ÷ RC, and of the three lines for the decay rule only dN ÷ N = −λ dt both separates and keeps the rule
The time constant for an RL circuit is L ÷ R: the coil's curve is drawn with τ = L ÷ R, and its worked lines give that time and the current one τ later

Equal times, equal fractions: a 1 s window reads 0.607 wherever it sits on the decay curve while both its voltages fall, its end arrow is shallower than its start arrow by that same share, and on the growth curve it reads 1.649 wherever it sits
Put back into the rule, v = 12 e^(−t/2) passes: the rider's two numbers, the curve's own slope and −v ÷ 2, agree at every time from 0 to 9.5 s, and both read −2.21 at 2 s
By this rule the voltage never quite reaches zero: for every RC from 0.5 s to 6 s the curve stays above 0 V all the way to 10 s, falling at every step

Every worked number is right: RC is 2 s, and 0.5 to 6 s on the sliders; the rates are −6 at 12 V, −3 at 6 V and −1.5 at 3 V, with the slips −6 and +1.5; the curve is at 4.41 V at 2 s, where the tangent from 12 V reaches zero; y = 5 e^(−2t) starts at a slope of −10 with τ = 0.5 s; the coil keeps 0.883 A, the slip 1.52 A; growth from 100 reaches about 272, the slips 200 and 36.8
Each puzzle accepts only its answer, draws it when it is checked, and draws every wrong pick as a mistake
Before Check, no puzzle's picture shows its answer or a mistake, and the window's readings at 6 s stay hidden
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, finishes within 2 s
